title: Trading Policy

tiers.name: Staff
tiers.description: All directors, officers, senior executives and other employees of the Group, other than those who are Directors or nominated as Designated Persons. May deal at any time provided they do not hold Inside Information and are not involved in short-term or speculative dealing; not subject to black-out periods or prior notification.

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: Umbrella term (section 3.3) for directors, the senior executive team and other persons nominated by the General Counsel and Company Secretary; Schedule 1 further splits this pool by office (Chairman, Managing Director, Executive/Non-Executive Directors, Director of Compliance, other nominated Staff) only to fix which Authorisation Officer clears their trades. Subject to black-out periods, prior notification/approval of Company Securities dealings, the third-party financial products restriction (4.1) and the unvested Plan hedging ban (4.2).

definitions.hedging_definition: financial products which operate to limit the economic risk of the unvested Company Securities issued under a Plan

windows.start_anchor: 31 December (end of the Company's financial year)
windows.end_anchor: release of the Company's annual results announcement to ASX
release of the Company's half-year results announcement to ASX

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Managing Director may declare other black-out periods from time to time. The Policy does not state whether these are announced or kept confidential.

rules.detail: Third-party financial products over BFG Securities (including bank-issued OTC instruments) are expressly addressed and named, but only barred if the dealing would independently breach insider trading, market rigging or misleading/deceptive conduct laws. This sits outside the black-out/prior-notification regime, which under 3.1 is limited to dealing in the Company's own Securities (shares and options), so no clearance is otherwise required.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons are not permitted to deal at any time in financial products designed to track, hedge or in any other way take a position associated with the future value of the Company's Securities (including options, warrants, futures or other financial products issued over the Company's Securities by third parties such as banks and other institutions) if such dealings would breach applicable laws

rules.detail: Absolute, clearance-free ban on hedging arrangements that limit the economic risk of unvested Company Securities issued under a Plan.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons must not enter into a transaction or arrangement or otherwise deal in financial products which operate to limit the economic risk of the unvested Company Securities issued under a Plan.

rules.detail: The 4.2 hedging ban is limited to unvested Plan securities; hedging vested Plan securities or ordinary shares falls back to clause 4.1's conditional third-party financial products rule, which permits it unless the dealing independently breaches insider trading, market rigging or misleading conduct laws.
rules.evidence: financial products designed to track, hedge or in any other way take a position associated with the future value of the Company's Securities ... if such dealings would breach applicable laws

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but a prepaid forward or similar arrangement with a bank is a third-party financial product taking a position associated with the future value of BFG Securities, so it falls within 4.1 and is permitted unless it independently breaches insider trading, market rigging or misleading conduct laws.
rules.evidence: financial products designed to track, hedge or in any other way take a position associated with the future value of the Company's Securities (including options, warrants, futures or other financial products issued over the Company's Securities by third parties such as banks and other institutions)

rules.detail: Short selling is not named or defined anywhere in the Policy.
Securities lending is not named anywhere in the Policy.

CFDs are not named but are a financial product taking a position associated with the future value of BFG Securities issued by a third party, so they fall within 4.1 and are permitted unless they independently breach insider trading, market rigging or misleading conduct laws.
rules.evidence: financial products designed to track, hedge or in any other way take a position associated with the future value of the Company's Securities (including options, warrants, futures or other financial products issued over the Company's Securities by third parties such as banks and other institutions)

rules.detail: Margin lending is not mentioned anywhere in this Policy.
Encumbering, charging or pledging Company Securities is not mentioned anywhere in this Policy.
The Policy contains no secured financing, collateral or margin loan provision of any kind.

Ordinary Staff (not Directors or Designated Persons) may deal at any time only if not involved in short-term or speculative dealing; the concept is named but undefined (no period, LIFO basis or intention test given).
rules.evidence: If you are not a director or Designated Person you can deal in the Company's Securities at any time provided you do not have Inside Information and are not involved in short-term or speculative dealing.

clearance.approver: Authorisation Officer per Schedule 1 (Chairman of the Audit Committee for the Chairman, Managing Director, Executive Directors and Non-Executive Directors; another Independent Non-Executive Director for the Chairman of the Audit Committee; the Executive Chairman or an Independent Non-Executive Director for the Director of Compliance; various senior officers for other nominated Staff), via a request submitted to the General Counsel and Company Secretary
clearance.evidence: Directors and Designated Persons must submit a request in the form of Schedule 3 to the General Counsel and Company Secretary, who will seek approval from the relevant Authorisation Officer (as defined in Schedule 1). Any approval given will be valid for seven days from the date it is given.

short_term.evidence: you can deal in the Company's Securities at any time provided you do not have Inside Information and are not involved in short-term or speculative dealing

exceptions.evidence: acquisitions of the Company's Securities (as applicable) under the relevant issue or Plan; or the exercise of any other entitlement under the relevant issue or Plan are permitted during a black-out period, subject to the provisions of the Trust Deed governing the Company's Employee Share Trust and the relevant Plan rules.

applications to participate in the relevant issue or Plan; or variations of instructions in relation to levels of participation in the relevant issue or Plan, may be made at any time whether or not within a black-out period

exceptions.approver: Chairman (for directors); General Counsel and Company Secretary (for Designated Persons)
exceptions.evidence: a director or Designated Person, who would otherwise be restricted by this policy, is in severe financial difficulty or there are other exceptional circumstances ... approval may be given by the Authorisation Officer in their discretion to allow a Designated Person to dispose of (but not acquire) Company Securities during a black-out period.

external_documents: Trust Deed governing the Company's Employee Share Trust
exemption_authority: The Authorisation Officer (Chairman for directors, General Counsel and Company Secretary for Designated Persons) may, in their discretion, approve disposal only (not acquisition) of Company Securities during a black-out period for severe financial difficulty or other exceptional circumstances, provided the person confirms in advance in writing that they hold no Inside Information. There is no equivalent discretion to approve an acquisition, a hedge of unvested Plan securities, or any dealing while in possession of Inside Information, which remain overriding prohibitions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons are not permitted to deal at any time in financial products designed to track, hedge or in any other way take a position associated with the future value of the Company's Securities (including options, warrants, futures or other financial products issued over the Company's Securities by third parties such as banks and other institutions) if such dealings would breach applicable laws.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A funded collar (put and call) with a bank is squarely a 'financial product issued over the Company's Securities by third parties such as banks' under 4.1, which is only prohibited if it independently breaches insider trading, market rigging or misleading conduct laws; there is no separate clearance, black-out or notification gate on the derivative legs themselves.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban limited to unvested plan securities
bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must not enter into a transaction or arrangement or otherwise deal in financial products which operate to limit the economic risk of the unvested Company Securities issued under a Plan.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The absolute hedging ban only reaches unvested Plan securities, so a collar over vested Plan shares or ordinary on-market shares is not caught by this clause and falls back to the more permissive conditional rule in 4.1.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy contains no clause addressing margin lending, encumbrance, collateral or any other secured financing arrangement in respect of Company Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, has no express policy bar, clearance requirement or notification obligation under this document, though it predates the hedging/derivatives drafting common in more recent ASX policies and the bank should confirm no newer version has since been adopted.

bespoke_clauses.topic: black-out and notification for the share leg
bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Designated Persons must submit a request in the form of Schedule 3 ... Any approval given will be valid for seven days.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the structure requires the executive to deal directly in BFG shares or options (e.g. delivering shares against the loan or into a custody arrangement), that dealing needs prior written notification and Authorisation Officer approval valid for only 7 days, and cannot occur in the two annual black-out periods absent a hardship-based sale approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Approved by the Board on 26 October 2010.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is a 2010 policy predating common ASX hedging and derivatives drafting; the bank should check BFG's current website version before relying on the permissive 4.1 analysis.

summary: On the face of this 2010 Trading Policy, a funded collar over vested BFG shares is unusually open: clause 4.1 expressly contemplates third-party financial products, including bank-issued instruments, that hedge or take a position on the future value of BFG Securities, and bars them only if the dealing would independently breach insider trading, market rigging or misleading conduct laws; there is no dedicated clearance, notification or black-out gate for the derivative legs, since the notification regime in 3.5 is limited to dealing in the Company's own Securities (shares and options). The absolute hedging ban in clause 4.2 reaches only unvested Plan securities, so it does not apply to a collar over vested or on-market shares. The Policy is entirely silent on margin lending, encumbrance or any other secured financing arrangement, so the loan leg secured on the collared shares also has no express policy bar, though this is a 2010 document and the bank should check for a more recent, unpublished version. If the structure requires the Designated Person to deal directly in BFG shares or options (for example, delivering shares into a custody or pledge arrangement), that dealing needs prior written notification to the General Counsel and Company Secretary, Authorisation Officer approval valid for 7 days, and must avoid the two annual black-out periods absent a hardship-based sale approval. Overall, a funded collar appears permitted subject to general law compliance and, for the underlying share leg only, the ordinary notification and black-out process.
